hype_moment: DGainz-channel video (Mar 11, 2012) hit 30M+ views before its Aug 2013 takedown; Kanye's remix landed May 1, 2012, seven weeks later, and Interscope paid $6M inside six months.

Dropped Oct 18, 2012 and a late-2012 report already cited ~20M YouTube views, roughly 20M in two months; the DGainz upload sits at 383M today (proxy: the ~20M figure is real but its date is unpinned).
Two unsigned 16-year-olds never charted, did ~10M views in the breakout window (unconfirmed on second pass) and 50M+ since, and Drake called them "the future" within months (proxy).

Video sat dormant from Mar 28, 2014 until Vine user Vladimir Francois looped the Shmoney Dance in June; 5M YouTube views in a single month, Beyoncé doing the dance on tour by July 15, a rumored $2M Epic deal and #1 Hot R&B/Hip-Hop.
"I'm in love with the coco" became a four-word Vine punchline detached from the record; no dated loop count survives (proxy: Hot 100 top-20 peak, exact position unverified).
Two opening bars sized for a six-second loop sold 785,562 US copies by July 2015, about two months after the May 4 release, and took a total unknown to #9 on the Hot 100.
Independent release May 12, 2016; 57M+ YouTube views and 32M Spotify plays by Oct 2016 with 400–500K daily US plays, #21 Hot 100 in eight chart weeks, and radio's 150K spins came after the views.
The audio had almost 1M YouTube views before an official video existed (FADER, Aug 12, 2016), Meek Mill and DJ Khaled shouted it out, and Drake brought him out on the Summer Sixteen tour in New York.
Drake told Coach K he'd been listening "for the last four days" and was on the remix a week later; the whole genre adopted the triplet flow while the single peaked at #99 (proxy: co-sign lag).
The Jan 2014 street record that preceded the radio single "Stoner"; praised by Drake and Kanye and remixed by Nicki Minaj within the year (proxy: co-sign lag).
Drake tweeted his remix Aug 12, 2014; Makonnen was signed to OVO Sound by Aug 31 (19 days) and the label single chased the co-sign on Sept 1.
Video Aug 28, 2014; 9M+ Vine loops, 16M+ YouTube plays and ~7M SoundCloud plays by Dec 2014, a 2 Chainz remix 29 days after upload, all on a #90 Hot 100 peak.
Recorded and released May 27, 2016, the day after he walked out of federal prison; the same-day turnaround was the event (proxy: no first-day view count recoverable).
July 14, 2016 lead single, Savage Mode a day later; XXL Freshman momentum into 2x Platinum and a pit staple all summer (proxy: no velocity data).

~100 "raindrop, drop top" tweets on release day became ~600,000 posts by Jan 2, 2017 (82% after Dec 7); Donald Glover's Globes shout-out drove a +243% Spotify spike, 32M+ streams the week ending Jan 14, #1 on Jan 21.
An album cut the fans chose: #MaskOffChallenge (recorders, violins, trombones) bubbled from early March and took off the week of Mar 30, 2017; certified gold by Apr 10, ~8 weeks after release.
Released June 9, 2015 to silence; one "Stop It, Joe" Vine on Feb 6, 2016 pulled ~8.6M loops, 212K likes and 80K revines in three months and made "I am the one" the sound of 2016 Vine.
SoundCloud Aug 19, 2015; a Feb 2016 Caleon Fox Vine skit "blew up on every social media platform within hours" and the track sits at 39M+ SoundCloud plays.

Rojas's SoundCloud, Dec 30, 2015; Drake's "KMT" flow controversy sent it onto the Hot 100 at #94 (Feb 25, 2017) then #34, 76M+ SoundCloud streams, and the May 6, 2017 Rolling Loud set had security pulling him from the pit.

SoundCloud Dec 15, 2015 (1M+ plays, "lightly viral"); Kanye built "Father Stretch My Hands Pt. 2" on it Feb 14, 2016; 22.3M US weekly streams (+48% w/w), 38.5M weekly by May 28, #1 Hot 100 May 7, 2016.
SoundCloud Mar 16, 2016; on Billboard's Spotify Velocity and Viral 50 charts by year-end, 76M streams by March 2017 with zero radio (DJBooth: "further proof radio is broken").
Leaked to SoundCloud Feb 26, 2017 with no art or video: 6.64M+ plays in two weeks, SoundCloud's #1 song of 2017 at 148M (5.5x the top pop song), 1.3B streams across platforms by Sept 2017.

The April 14, 2017 single the fans picked off the mixtape; Complex named it a Song of the Summer contender within a month, Jay-Z called it "incredible," Kimmel debut in June (proxy: no stream count recovered).
Uploaded June 2017 while he was a fugitive (US Marshals arrested him the day it dropped); 10M+ YouTube views and a Billboard chart entry within a month.
Ben Griffin video Oct 23, 2017 gained 75M+ views in three weeks, the biggest 21-day YouTube figure in the research; 108M+ combined Spotify/YouTube streams by late October.
648,029 first-week YouTube views (low-confidence source) became 29M+ in a month; 100M+ SoundCloud streams and #1 on SoundCloud's chart for all of Dec 2017–Jan 2018.
SoundCloud June 15, 2017; 2M+ plays got a $3M Interscope deal (Mar 2018) after exactly one public show; Cole Bennett video May 11, 2018; SoundCloud's #1 track of 2018 at 123M plays.
Surprise diss July 29, 2015 debuted at #21 Hot 100; five days later the OVO Fest crowd chanted it "like it was his biggest Platinum hit."
TLOP premiered live from Madison Square Garden Feb 14, 2016; Tidal claimed 250M streams in 10 days (disputed) and the album became the first to hit #1 primarily on streaming.
No-warning video Mar 30, 2017 did ~500,000 YouTube views in 90 minutes; 49.8M US streams on the chart dated Apr 22, 2017 (the "Spotify day-one record" claim could not be verified).
DAMN. did 50M+ streams in its first 24 hours (Apr 14, 2017) and 340.6M in week one, 2017's biggest; the beat switch became the era's purest rage cue.

SoundCloud June 16, 2017 "without record label or radio support"; after a year of crowd-video spread it debuted at #82 (Sept 8, 2018) and climbed 76 spots to #6 in about eight weeks (delayed detonation, community-first).
ASTROWORLD did 64.5M day-one US Apple Music streams (Aug 3, 2018); the song did 55.1M streams in release week and #1 on Apple/Spotify US, then took a 17-week climb to Hot 100 #1.
SoundCloud Aug 21, 2017; the WorldStar premiere Sept 18, 2017 pulled 22M+ views in four weeks, an Alabama gamer kid's first-ever video.
Lyrical Lemonade Oct 18, 2017; Skies signed to Atlantic the same season off the "i"/"Nowadays"/"Red Roses" run (proxy: signing lag; 251M+ views by Oct 2022).

WSHH video July 5, 2018; the "Respect My Cryppin'" meme (Oct 2018) back-propagated onto it, Cole Bennett's YG remix video (Jan 25, 2019) did 11M+ views in a few weeks and it debuted at #75 the next day.
Self-released Jan 2019: 915,000 views in week one, 10M in a month, and a three-way $3M bidding war (Republic/Interscope/Caroline) inside 30 days, which the 16-year-old turned down.
Video Jan 13, 2019 did 2M+ views in four days; Columbia had the single out by Feb 1, about three weeks later.
Self-directed video Mar 4, 2019 passed 100M views by ~July 6 (~4 months) and 185M+ by year-end; Billboard convened a staff roundtable when it cracked the top 40.
Lyrical Lemonade May 22, 2019: 21M+ views in under a month, Hot 100 debut at #93 three weeks after upload, 3.3M Spotify streams a day in late August, #4 peak in ~8 weeks.

artist: Juice WRLD ft. YoungBoy Never Broke Again
hype_moment: Lyrical Lemonade Oct 4, 2019: 2.4M views in just over 12 hours and #2 on YouTube Trending, the best sub-24-hour figure in the era.
Recorded the day he left prison; the Nov 7, 2016 video did 2M views in under three weeks, and LeBron James rapping it on camera spawned the "LeBron James Challenge."
July 25, 2017 closet recording; the dance went from Frayser mirrors to Fortnite ("Hype," May 2018) and a lawsuit against Epic on only ~5.5M official video views.
The shoot dance got so big Drake showed up to learn it on camera; released Feb 8, 2018 and debuted at #6 on the Hot 100.
WSHH upload Oct 8, 2018 did 2M views in a month; the offbeat flow hit Twitter and made him a meme before he was a rapper.
Apr 23, 2019; spread through Instagram "within weeks," took over New York, Nicki Minaj (Aug 15) and Skepta (Aug 21) remixes inside one week, multimillion-dollar deal (proxy: no first-week count).
June 5, 2019; lived in Instagram Stories until it was worth a multimillion-dollar deal; >7M Spotify / >12M YouTube at interview time (proxy: modest raw numbers).
Self-released July 30, 2020; Warner signed and re-released it after the TikTok run; #10 Hot 100 by Feb 2021, #3 UK (proxy: signing lag).
Nov 6, 2020; reached #13 Hot 100 and #2 Rap Streaming Songs before a video existed (video Jan 2, 2021); now 8x Platinum.
Never a single, no launch video; TikTok keyed on the "eee-urr" squeak mid-Dec 2019; 32M US streams in its first week, 68.2M the week ending Jan 9, 2020, 1.5M TikTok videos, 11 weeks at #1.
Keara Wilson posted her dance five days running before it caught; 15.7M views / 2.4M likes by Mar 20, 2020, Megan's own version Mar 16; TikTok's most-played song of March 2020.
Aug 14, 2020; @ohbukster's challenge produced 5.8M TikTok videos and 1.3B sound plays; #92 debut, Nicki Minaj remix Oct 16 pushed it to #35.
Whole Lotta Red dropped Christmas Day 2020: #1 on Twitter, three of YouTube's top-10 trending slots, 112.1M US streams and 100,000 units in one week, and a fanbase that argued about it for a year.
Sept 1, 2021; the bell became the meme, Drake, Lil Yachty and Druski quoted it, and it barely charted with zero radio (proxy: the Chartmetric case study was blocked).
Aug 27, 2021: Kendrick's first verse since 2018 at 2am with no warning; Keem's first top-20 and a Best Rap Performance Grammy (proxy: no day-one figure recovered).
Apr 29, 2022; "labels started calling the following morning," #FNFChallenge 9M+ views, 399,000+ TikTok creations, CMG deal in ~10 weeks on a #42 peak.
Dropped June 28, 2022 inside a Lyrical Lemonade Minions trailer; 2.4M+ TikTok videos and the GentleMinions theater phenomenon; #38 Hot 100.
Aug 10, 2022; Drake played it on OVO Sound Radio, flew her to Toronto and posted her on his IG story within a month; #munch 2B+ TikTok views.
Oct 17, 2022; TikToks using it collected 500M views within three weeks; #10 Hot 100 and #1 Hot Rap Songs.
Jan 27, 2023; broke during Miami spring break with no usable radio edit; 250,000+ TikTok clips.
June 9, 2023 ad-lib became all-purpose comedy audio; #1 on the inaugural TikTok Billboard Top 50 (Sept 14, 2023) and Rolling Stone's #1 rap song of 2023.
UTOPIA (July 28, 2023) had Apple Music's biggest first-day of 2023; "FE!N" debuted with 25.6M streams and its run-it-back live ritual became the era's signature bit.
Mar 22, 2024: 59.6M US streams in week one (2024's biggest week), 91M global, #1 Hot 100 debut, a three-way war started inside 45 seconds of a surprise album.
Apr 30, 2024 YouTube-first audio drop: 9.206M opening-day Spotify streams, at the time the largest for any hip-hop song in 2024.

May 4, 2024: 10.986M Spotify streams day one, ~12.809M on day four (12.2M per KTT2) breaking "Girls Want Girls" 12.385M; video did 18–20M views in under 24h; performed five (or six) times at The Pop Out June 19.
